page: Microsoft Azure DS2_v2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the DSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.5 GB of RAM per core, and includes 14 GB of local storage. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX and AVX-512F, along with AES cryptography and BMI2 integer manipulation.

Benchmark data indicates that the DS2_v2 occupies the lower performance tiers. In CPU-bound workloads, the instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1246.49 and a multi-core score of 2467.38, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached large-block read bandwidth recorded at 22.78 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 18.09 GB/sec. The instance demonstrated weak performance in database operations with a Passmark database score of 1345.89 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.81 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the DS2_v2 is its limited processing and memory throughput, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1922.0 and a static web serving throughput of 2.52 GB/sec. However, it maintains average performance in specific tasks, such as LLM text generation using a small 135M model, which reached 94.89 tokens per second. Given its hardware profile and dedicated CPU allocation, the instance offers an entry-level option for lightweight workloads. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, basic utility applications, small-scale development environments, and simple background tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing.
